attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence. He cites The Information just before it, but this sentence is his own.

semantics.note: Keeps all three parts as written: Oracle's scale is new for Oracle, Crusoe has never done this, and OpenAI regularly underestimates demand. Stated flatly, so it is an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'never done this' as no prior comparable hyperscale campus is ordinary and fair. Requiring repeated demand surprises for 'regularly' is reasonable. The rule that Oracle building may mean tenant rather than developer is a real ambiguity.

evidence.note: Bisnow, dated before the cutoff: Crusoe is new to hyperscale development and its leadership admits no experience at Abilene's scale. Supports the Crusoe part. It also calls Oracle the tenant.
Altman admitted twice in a month (GPT-4.5 and image generation) that demand surges caused GPU shortfalls. Supports repeated demand surprises.

As of Sept 2024, Oracle's largest site, including those under construction, was 800MW, against 1.2GW planned at Abilene. This points toward a new scale, but it is not a full record through May 2025, and gigawatt builds were planned.
Crusoe press release showing earlier cloud and colocation work. This does not show a comparable campus delivered, so it does not refute the comparable-campus reading.

reviews.rationale: The Crusoe part is supported by e5. The OpenAI part is supported by two admitted demand-driven shortfalls in e6. The Oracle-scale part is only suggested by a Sept 2024 snapshot (e7). There is no complete record to May 2025, and Oracle's role as tenant rather than builder is unresolved. Two parts hold and one is not established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Insane' is rhetorical. The checkable core is that losses are growing while OpenAI commits to big projects. Faithful to the sentence.

contract.note: Reading 'deeper into the red' as rising absolute losses is the ordinary reading. The reporting window and the loss measure are the evaluator's choices, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: A projection made in 2024 of a roughly $5B loss that year. A forecast, not a series of actual results, so it cannot establish the trend.
OpenAI's own announcement shows its part in Stargate, with SoftBank carrying the financing. It documents one project, not the loss trend.
A summary of internal projections that flags unclear accounting for compute costs. No actual losses.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no consistent series of actual losses through March 2025. It holds only projections and a project announcement. Large losses are plausible, but the evidence cannot show losses increasing on any stated basis, and nothing contradicts the claim either.

attribution.note: Zitron's own aside in the newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps his hedge 'supposed $100 billion' and the claim that SoftBank has financial responsibility. A present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'trouble' as real obstacles or delays, not final failure, is ordinary. Reading 'full financial responsibility' as SoftBank's financing role fits the announcement's wording.

evidence.note: The joint announcement gives SoftBank financial responsibility. This supports the role part, which the contract says should rest on primary disclosure.
Report dated May 12, 2025, summarising Bloomberg: tariff uncertainty had stopped any SoftBank financing for the $100B going forward. It is in the target window.

reviews.rationale: The Stargate announcement gives SoftBank the financing role. Reporting from May 2025, within the window, describes stalled financing for the initial $100B because of tariffs and fears of oversupply. Both elements of the support condition are met. The only caveat is that the stall rests on one underlying Bloomberg report.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. The ChatGPT exception comes from his own sentence just before it.

semantics.note: Adding the ChatGPT exception from the sentence before is faithful. The claim is a flat statement that no real LLM consumer product exists besides ChatGPT.

contract.note: His own question about products from GPT and Gemini, and the ChatGPT exception, show he means software. Reading 'real' as substantive features plus shown consumer use is an ordinary reading, not stretched against him.

evidence.note: Google's own figure from May 20, 2025: the Gemini app has over 400M monthly users. The contract accepts company usage figures. It shows wide consumer use inside the window.
Google's notes from May 20, 2025 list Gemini app features available that day, such as Canvas, quizzes and Deep Research. These are substantive everyday functions.

reviews.rationale: Within the window, the Gemini app had substantive consumer features already available and over 400M monthly users, per Google's own figures. That meets the contradiction condition: an LLM consumer product other than ChatGPT with real use. One limit: the usage figures are Google's own and not independently checked.
